name: How long does a full kitchen remodel usually take from demo to completion, and what delays should I expect?

mainEntity.name: How long does a full kitchen remodel usually take from demo to completion, and what delays should I expect?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A typical full kitchen remodel takes about 8–14 weeks from demolition to completion once permits are issued and materials are on site. Larger or highly customized kitchens can take longer. 
Context: The schedule depends heavily on city inspections, lead times for cabinets and countertops, and how much structural or systems work is involved. Hidden issues (old wiring, damaged framing, asbestos) can add time. 
Key factors:
- Time to secure permits and any required engineering
- Cabinet and countertop fabrication lead times
- Availability of inspectors and subcontractors
- Change orders and unforeseen conditions during demo
Practical guidance: Ask your contractor for a written schedule with key milestones and a contingency buffer, and insist on weekly updates. Order long-lead items early and avoid mid-project design changes to keep the timeline on track. Soft positioning: An organized contractor will build realistic slack into the schedule and communicate early when delays pop up.
